root_cause.text: In panthor_fw_unplug(), the halt and wait-for-halt procedures were called unconditionally without checking whether the firmware (MCU) was loaded or initialized, causing a NULL pointer dereference when it was not.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that "the FW may not even be loaded/initialized at all, the latter of which can lead to a NULL pointer dereference." The patch removes the calls to panthor_fw_halt_mcu() and panthor_fw_wait_mcu_halted() because it is unsafe to invoke them when the FW state is unknown.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove halting and waiting for MCU halt during firmware unplug to fix potential hangs or unnecessary delays.
intent_record.what: Removed calls to panthor_fw_halt_mcu and panthor_fw_wait_mcu_halted (with warning on failure) from panthor_fw_unplug, so the firmware is stopped directly without an explicit halt.
intent_record.how: The firmware unplug path no longer halts the MCU and waits for it to halt before stopping the firmware; it now proceeds directly to panthor_fw_stop.

grouping_result.intent: Remove halting and waiting for MCU halt during firmware unplug to fix potential hangs or unnecessary delays.

relevance_review.reason: The group removes the halt and wait-for-halt calls in panthor_fw_unplug(), which directly addresses the root cause of unconditional halting leading to a NULL pointer dereference when firmware is not loaded.
